1 ¶ Stipula illectaa illecta sunt spicae Hal.Il-lecta dicitur stipula, quae nondum col-lecta. est spicae in messeb in messem Valgat. Hal. & male. In messe, id est, dum messis fieret. deleetae[?], nec dum lectae, quas rustici, cum vacauerintc occauerint, & male. sensus est, Spi-cas, quae post messorum terga a tenuioribus legi solent, stipulas appellari. colligunt.

main_text.head: 31. Ulpianus libro octauodecimo ad Edictum.
main_text.p: PlRatum est, in quo ad fructum percipiendum falce duntaxat opus est, ex eo dictum, quod pa-cas[?], quae post messorum terga a tenuioribus legi solent, stipulas appellari. Terentius in Adelphis: praeter hęc, meridie ipso, faciam ut stipulam colligat: huc refer
19. Lucit. vers. 9. [?] 22: Ruth. 2. verficul. 3. & 7. d [illegible, ~3 words] Eclog. ibid. c. 30. hinc illæ voces Nouelletum l. 39. 5. de hered. pet: nouellum l. 8.
5. de fundo dotali: noualis ager, Varro 4. de lingua: l. vlt. in f. 5. de termino. Nouale 18. Plin. 19: nouata terra Cicero de oratione.
e profcissa Hal. [illegible, ~1 word] Ecloga ibid. cap. 30.

Liber variorum auctorum de finitibus, nouialis ager dicitur, qui primum proscissus. & apud Seruium 1. Georgicon. Nouales, funt arua primum proscissa. Idem refert Hieronimus & Innocentius iii. in c. nouale 1. & 2. extra de verbor. fignif. vbi tractant interpretes, num ex nouali-bus debeantur decimæ. Ea res facit vt hic legendum putem. Noualis est etiâ terra primum procisa, & quæ anno cessauit. vt huius vocis duæ sint significationes.

Addatur tertia, vt nouale, fit ager, cuius vetus facies immutata fit in nouam, veteri non abfimilem. Vt fi vetus aliuetum fuccidas, vt nouellum reponas l. 8. 5. de fundo dotali: ex filua nouale facias l. vlt. 5. de termino, quod nihil aliud effe puto, quâ nouelletum in fundo facere l. 32. 5. de heredit. petit. l. 6. 5. de impenfis. fcio tamen Seruium 1. Ecloga fcribere nouaiia dici, vnde filua tollitur.

f quæ alternis annis cessauit nouandarum sibi virium causa. hinc illud Virgilij 1. Georgicon, Alternis idem tonsas cessaro nouales. page.notes: Long s normalised to plain s throughout. Printed hyphens at line ends kept (Hal.Il-lecta, col-lecta, cadu-ca, pa-cas, Spi-cas). Doubtful readings: "deleetae" (text, marked [?]); "pa-cas" in the Ratum paragraph, a line break that I could not resolve with certainty; "vnie" in the note h; the abbreviated Pascuis citation "asde iij" and its number. Greek fragments that could not be read reliably are marked illegible. The marker k in the text ("est k") has no matching footnote I could identify on this page, so it may be printed elsewhere or a misread. The marginal notes a, b and c are set in the right-hand column at the head of the page; the note c runs on into the full-width text. The footnote split into paragraphs follows the apparent breaks, which are hard to see at this scan resolution.
